faq_description: Clear explanations of the key things teams need to understand.
faq_accounts_question: Do employees need to create accounts?
faq_accounts_answer: No. A workplace can be open to anyone with the link or protected with a join code or private link. Access can be remembered on the device, which makes workhal practical on shared workplace computers and employees’ phones. An employee account is still recommended, though, because it lets managers assign roles and keep employee-specific data.
faq_difference_question: How is workhal different from Docs or Notion?
faq_difference_answer: Docs and Notion are flexible places to create pages. workhal is a ready-made employee portal: it starts with the workday, keeps published information separate from manager controls, connects guides to events and files, and gives staff one task-focused search across the workplace.
faq_content_answer: Use guides for repeatable tasks, the calendar for reservations, training, maintenance, and other operational dates, the document library for files and shared links, and common questions for fast everyday answers. Alongside these main features, workhal also includes smaller conveniences that make everyday work easier, such as personal notes for workers.
faq_maintainers_question: Can more than one person maintain the content?
faq_maintainers_answer: Yes. Give people view-only, editing, or full content access. Drafts stay out of the employee view until they are published, and the activity history shows who created, changed, or removed workplace content.
faq_gradual_question: Can we start without moving everything at once?
faq_gradual_answer: Yes. Start with the recurring answers, practical guides, and important dates the team needs most often, then add the rest at a pace the workplace can maintain.
